claim:rust-engine-in-workbench.proposition:
The Rust engine runs the bursting gene-expression benchmark as a workbench composite
(RustHybridStep bridging the real run_ir binary) and is ~30-50x faster than plain
interpreted Python per run.

claim:speedup-landscape.proposition:
Rust/numba stays 1.3-2.6x and is nearly flat in event density; the hybrid is faithful to
exact SSA only at stochastic_fraction = 1.0 (where it is the exact path).

claim:regime-frontier.proposition:
No. The only >=5x cells are large systems at low stochastic fraction (10.8x at size 100 /
fraction 0.1; 6.8x at fraction 0.25), and both FAIL fidelity (worst |z| ~14-17). The
faithful cells (stochastic_fraction = 1.0) are ~1.0x. Fast and trustworthy are disjoint.

narrative.question:
For what kinds of models does a pure-Rust hybrid ODE/SSA engine pay off, and
where does the hybrid partition stay accurate? The viva-hybrid trial measured a
single benchmark (Rust 2.01x vs numba -> MARGINAL); this investigation sweeps
model characteristics to map WHERE a Rust hybrid engine clears the >=5x bar AND
the hybrid approximation remains faithful to exact stochastic simulation.

decisions.title: Sweep copy number / species abundance as an axis?
decisions.detail:
Copy numbers were held low (~10-30), a regime where deterministic treatment of
a continuous species is a poor approximation by construction. High-copy
continuous species would be well-approximated deterministically and could open a
faithful-and-fast window. Copy number is the single most likely axis to change
the verdict and was not swept - the recommended next investigation.
